title: The projective line is a regular Noetherian one-dimensional scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\mathbf P^1_k=\operatorname{Proj}k[x_0,x_1]$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. Then $\mathbf P^1_k$ is a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), it is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], and its dimension [def-pc-dimension] is $1$.

source.place: Example Tag 01JE (schemes-example-projective-line), together with the standard dimension and regularity assertions for projective space

proof.text: Use the standard affine cover $X=U_0\cup U_1$ with $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ from [def-sc-p1-standard]. Each affine spectrum is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii), and a finite union of quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. The coordinate rings are Noetherian by [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-noetherian], so the definition [pqf-def-locnoeth] gives that $X$ is locally Noetherian and hence Noetherian.

Every point of $X$ lies in one of the two affine charts. On either chart the ring is a polynomial ring in one variable over $k$, hence regular by [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-regular]. Therefore each point has an affine neighbourhood with Noetherian regular coordinate ring, which is exactly the defining condition [def-weil-regular-scheme] for $X$ to be regular.

source.place: Example Tag 01JE (schemes-example-projective-line), regularity from standard charts

proof.text: For a point $x$ in a chart $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a localization $(A_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ at the corresponding prime by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Its dimension is the height of $\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], and this is at most $\dim A_i$ by [lem-pc-ring-dimension-supremum-heights]. Since $A_i\cong k[t]$ or $k[s]$ and [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-dimension-one] gives dimension one, every local ring has dimension at most one. At the point corresponding to the prime $(t)\subset k[t]$, the strict chain $(0)\subsetneq(t)$ shows the local ring has dimension at least one, so $\dim X=1$ by [def-pc-dimension].

source.place: Lemma Tags 00KG and 00OQ, applied to the two standard affine charts

proof.text: The conclusions of Steps 1--3 are respectively quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, regular, and dimension exactly one; unfolding the definitions of Noetherian scheme, regular scheme, and [def-pc-dimension] yields all clauses of the statement.

lean.statement: theorem noetherian_regular_dim_one (k : Type u) [Field k] : let X := ProjectiveLine (Spec (.of k)) CompactSpace X ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧ (∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ (U : X.Opens) ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) ∧ X.dim = 1
